item.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Once-Weekly Semaglutide 2.4 mg in Korean Adults With Obesity or Overweight: A Multicenter Retrospective Real-World Study (RE-SEMA-K Study)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide 2.4 mg achieved substantial weight loss in South Korean adults with overweight or obesity. Weight reduction was comparable to the STEP 6 trial despite shorter follow-up (4.9 months), substantial prior obesity medication exposure, and accelerated dose escalation, supporting robust real-world effectiveness.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study established a comprehensive algorithm for endoscopic forehead mass excision. This study supports international PCOS guidelines that recommend screening and managing OSA.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Despite comparable visual and refractive outcomes, the three procedures produced distinct corneal optical profiles. TGL minimized coma and total HOA induction across most zones, whereas TGL and KLEx induced less peripheral SA and a smaller oblate shift than CQL. The largest differences arose at 6.0 and 7.0 mm, the former within the mesopic pupil of most patients; their effect on visual function was not assessed.

item.title: Ab-interno Ripcord Reinsertion for Overfiltration-related Hypotony After A-stream Glaucoma Shunt Surgery
item.description: CONCLUSION: Ab-interno ripcord reinsertion is a feasible and conjunctiva-sparing technique for resolving persistent overfiltration-related hypotony following ripcord removal or loss after A-stream glaucoma shunt implantation. Close postoperative IOP monitoring is warranted, as restoration of intraluminal resistance may result in IOP elevation requiring additional intervention in some patients.

item.title: Post-loading Polypoidal Lesion Height and Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography-Defined Regression in Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Lower post-loading polypoidal lesion height on B-mode OCT was associated with OCTA-defined regression after anti-VEGF loading therapy. Although the identified cutoff requires validation, post-loading polypoidal lesion height may serve as a practical, accessible OCT-based structural biomarker for estimating OCTA-defined regression during routine clinical follow-up.

item.title: Multiparametric Transperineal Ultrasound Features of Perianal Fistulas in Pediatric Crohn's Disease: From Baseline to Radiologic Healing
item.description: CONCLUSION: Radiologic healing in pediatric perianal Crohn disease is characterized by distinct multiparametric TPUS changes, including diameter reduction, loss of layered pattern, emergence of anisotropy, and resolution of inflammatory markers. While TPUS serves as a valuable adjunct to MRI for assessing treatment response, the persistent sonographic detectability of fistulas despite MRI-defined healing warrants further validation in larger cohorts and long-term follow-up studies.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Diabetes-related distress is common in people with type 1 diabetes and other forms of PED, with emotional burden being particularly prominent. Higher DDS scores were associated with more favorable views of disability registration, suggesting that perceived psychosocial burden may influence perspectives on formal recognition and support.

item.title: Discovery of Small-Molecule Cryoprotectants Using Pretrained Language Model Representations
item.description: Cryopreservation supports cell therapy, transfusion medicine, and tissue banking, but cryoprotectant selection remains constrained by empirical screening, toxicity, and ice recrystallization. We used pretrained language models as SMILES sequence encoders to prioritize small-molecule cryoprotectants for experimental testing. Hierarchical representations were coupled to descriptor reconstruction, gated fusion, and downstream prediction of normalized mean grain size and thresholded labels....
